subject: Orbitas Health — incident timeline, credit request, and next steps
body:
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@orbitas.health>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rajiv Patel <rajiv.patel@orbitas.health>, procurement@orbitas.health
Date: Fri, 1 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production incident May 1 — elevated 5xx/429 affecting ingestion pipeline

Rishi,

We experienced a significant spike in 5xx and 429 responses between 08:43–09:35 PDT this morning. Our ingestion workers retried aggressively and we observed request backlogs and timeouts in our downstream systems. This caused a ~18% drop in processed throughput for the morning window and a number of time-sensitive records were delayed.

Can you provide an incident timeline, an explanation for why our retries caused a cascading failure, and an estimate for credits under our SLA? Procurement is asking for an initial position by EOD today.

Thanks,
Elena Torres
Head of Platform Operations
Orbitas Health

---

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@orbitas.health>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 1 May 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production incident May 1 — elevated 5xx/429 affecting ingestion pipeline

Hi Elena — thanks for the note and I’m sorry for the disruption. I’ve looped in our incident and customer success leads so we can respond with timelines and a proposed credit calculation. Immediate items:

- Can you confirm how many requests/minute your ingestion service was sending during the peak window?
- Were retries standard exponential backoff or a custom aggressive retry?

We’ll share an initial timeline within 4 hours and a compensation proposal by EOD. I’ll escalate to my director if we need credits beyond standard SLA terms.

Rishi
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

---

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Elena Torres <elena.torres@orbitas.health>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 1 May 2026 12:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production incident May 1 — elevated 5xx/429 affecting ingestion pipeline

Elena — we pulled logs and have attachments (orbitas_error_logs_20260501.tar.gz). Quick summary:

- 08:41 PDT: upstream spike in request rate from Orbitas; 9x baseline for ~7 minutes.
- 08:48–09:10 PDT: our autoscaler successfully added capacity but a configuration mismatch allowed a small subset of long-lived connections to exhaust per-host concurrency limits, causing 502/504 responses and 429s as the edge rejected additional requests.
- 09:15 PDT: retry storms observed — several clients (including your ingestion workers) retried without jitter which amplified load.
- 09:35 PDT: fallback routing kicked in and traffic normalized; recovery completed by ~09:45 PDT.

We’re compiling a timeline and RCA. For now, we propose a provisional credit equal to 20% of the May invoice for the affected ingestion-metrics route, pending final RCA and contract terms. That’s an initial offering to avoid escalation while we finish the root-cause analysis.

Marissa
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

---

From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@orbitas.health>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rajiv Patel <rajiv.patel@orbitas.health>, procurement@orbitas.health
Date: Fri, 1 May 2026 13:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production incident May 1 — incident timeline, credit request, and next steps

Marissa — thanks for the quick work. Orbitas runs time-sensitive measures for patient monitoring; a 20% provisional credit is a reasonable start but procurement will need a formal statement of impacted SLA clauses and the exact credit calculation.

We need:
- Formal timeline that attributes which errors were service-side vs client-side retry amplification.
- A written mitigation plan to prevent similar retry storms (server-side rate limiting, guidance on client retry jitter, and concurrency headers).
- A draft credit calculation we can attach to our internal incident report.

We also have a contract clause that allows executive-level exceptions for repeat infra failures. If the RCA shows configuration mismatch on Redwood’s side, we will escalate to our CRO for additional credits.

Elena

---

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Elena Torres <elena.torres@orbitas.health>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 2 May 2026 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production incident May 1 — incident timeline, credit request, and next steps

Elena — adding more detail from the SRE review and attaching a draft SLA credit spreadsheet (sla_credit_calc_v1.xlsx). Key technical points:

- Root cause: a canary release changed connection pool behavior for one of the edge clusters. The release passed unit tests but the pool ceiling interaction with Orbitas’ high-concurrency ingestion pattern created a window where backpressure resulted in 502/504.
- Retry amplification: client-side retries without jitter increased qps by ~40% during the tail of the peak. We recognize this should have been caught by release gating and we’re instituting an extra release check against high-concurrency traffic shapes.
- Proposed remediation: rollback the Canary config, add per-customer concurrency safeguards, and publish updated retry guidance with recommended jitter/backoff.

Provisional credit calc (in the spreadsheet):
- Affected window: 1.07 hours (08:41–09:45)
- Measured impact: 18% reduction in processed throughput for ingestion route
- Credit recommendation: 20% of monthly billing for impacted route pro-rated to 1.07 hours = 0.9% of monthly invoice.

We’re happy to escalate to discounts beyond standard SLA if RCA shows we introduced config risk; that will need director review.

Sean
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

---

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@orbitas.health>, Rajiv Patel <rajiv.patel@orbitas.health>, procurement@orbitas.health
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Stephanie_Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 3 May 2026 17:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Orbitas incident — formal offer and next steps

Elena / Rajiv / Procurement team — thank you for the patience while we completed an internal review. Attached is a formal offer (sla_draft_redline_v2.pdf) and the credit calculation (sla_credit_calc_v1.xlsx). Summary of our offer:

- We accept responsibility for the canary configuration change that reduced per-host concurrency under a specific traffic shape.
- Immediate actions we’ve taken: rollback of the Canary, added per-customer soft limits to prevent cascading, and a release-gating test for high-concurrency patterns.
- Compensation: a one-time credit equal to 5% of the May invoice for the impacted route, plus a further 10% goodwill credit applied to June invoice if Orbitas signs the enclosed SLA addendum within 10 business days. Total potential credit = 15% (5% immediate + 10% contingent).
- Next steps: sign the SLA addendum or propose edits via DocuSign link; we’ll schedule a post-mortem call with your platform team next week to walk technical mitigations and recommended client retry changes.

Please reply with acceptance or counter-offer. If this requires executive engagement from our side we can escalate; otherwise Marissa and Sean will run the technical follow-through.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0142

--
Attachments: sla_draft_redline_v2.pdf; sla_credit_calc_v1.xlsx; orbitas_error_logs_20260501.tar.gz
